topic.title: Turtle Square Challenge
topic.description: Draws a square by repeating forward and right-turn movements in a for loop. A focused challenge connecting loop logic with turtle geometry.

learningNotes.whatILearned: Four sides of equal length: forward, turn a quarter, and do it four times.
learningNotes.challenges: The square is drawn and then the window closes before anyone can see it.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Add the screen and `exitonclick()` — without them this file produces nothing you can look at.

files.description: Draws a square using a for loop.

misconceptions: Turning right four times by 90 degrees comes back to where you started — the square is the *sum* of the turns, not the shape of any one of them
A drawing program has to keep its window open, or the drawing is a flash
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 20 + 0 = 20%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter` — so the 40 points for *it runs* are
not ones I can give, and they are not given. The other two bands are judged
by reading the code, carefully, line by line.

There is a bigger point here, and it is worth saying plainly: **`tkinter`
does not exist on Termux either.** These files cannot be run on the phone
this whole system is built around. They are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

The geometry is right: forward, right 90, forward, right 90, four times over, and the turtle ends up back at the start having drawn a square. The numbers are the right numbers.

**What is not**

**It produces nothing you can see.** There is no `Screen()` and no `exitonclick()`, so the window opens and closes in the same instant and the square is gone before it exists. As a file in the archive it is a drawing that nobody has ever seen.

There is also no comment explaining why four sides of 90 degrees close the shape — which is the one idea in the file.

**The one thing to fix first**

```python
from turtle import Turtle, Screen
...
screen = Screen()
screen.exitonclick()  # Keep the window open, or the square vanishes.
```

Then one comment: *four turns of 90 degrees bring the turtle back to the start, which is why the shape closes.*
